correctness.rationale: For every mixed edge with mutant count a and resident count b, directly summing parent choices gives drift r^{-i}G_{a,b}(r)/(dZ); G(1)=G'(1)=0 and G''(r)=ab[(b-1)r^{-b-1}+(a-1)r^{a-2}]>0 for a+b>=3. Each mixed configuration crosses some hyperedge, so Y_t=r^{-I_t} is bounded with strictly positive conditional drift. Connected finite-state chain absorbs a.s. by positive-probability mutant-spreading paths. At absorption, E[Y_tau]=(1-p)+p r^{-N}, implying strict Moran inequality with sign correct on both sides of 1. Neutral mutant count is a martingale. Ordinary regular pairwise graphs yield zero drift and equality. Exact rational verifier.py completed 8112 assertions, including exact absorption and published 4-5 vertex values.

value.rationale: The new universal theorem replaces case-by-case numerical evidence for regular higher-order full-group selection suppression with a structural all-fitness/all-configuration guarantee, including nonuniform group sizes and a sharp ordinary-graph equality boundary. It answers an explicit mechanism-driven mathematical issue in the initiating 2023 study and eliminates exponential Markov solving for determining suppression sign on an entire natural graph class. This is not a mere recomputation of a finite known table.
